prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: Legal, IP, regulatory.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Patent suits and ITC investigations (named parties, products at risk of import bans), antitrust cases, major court rulings, SEC/DOJ/FTC enforcement, foreign regulator probes of US companies (China SAMR/SASAC/MOFCOM, EU) — named companies.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **FSLR** / JA Solar / Corning [Specialty Materials & IP Licensing]
- First Solar filed a patent-infringement lawsuit on October 2 against JA Solar Technology, JA Solar International, JA Solar Vietnam, JA Solar Industrial and American Panel Solutions, a Corning subsidiary, in the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware; the complaint alleges infringement of U.S. Patent No. 9,130,074 concerning TOPCon crystalline-silicon solar-cell manufacturing methods. The case was pending as of October 5 at 12:20 ET; no import-ban order was reported. (NewsQuawk, Oct. 5 10:16 ET; Now.Solar, Oct. 4 02:00 ET)

## **NVDA** / Greg Lui [AI Compute]
- California businessman Greg Lui was charged by U.S. prosecutors with conspiracy, smuggling and money laundering over allegations that he routed servers containing more than $300 million of Nvidia AI chips to China through Malaysia and Singapore using false documentation; the criminal case was reported on October 2, with no conviction reported by October 5 at 12:20 ET. [report] (NewsQuawk citing Bloomberg, Oct. 5 10:16 ET)

## **ANTHROPIC**, **OPENAI**, METR [AI Infrastructure]
- The Federal Trade Commission opened an industry-wide probe into Anthropic, OpenAI and other AI laboratories over potential consumer harms from AI agents; an FTC official said the agency planned formal information demands and compelled executive testimony, including from Anthropic, OpenAI and METR. The investigation was active as of October 5 at 12:20 ET. (The Business Standard citing Reuters, Oct. 5 08:50 ET)

## Crypto firms / OCC [Crypto]
- The Independent Community Bankers of America sued the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency on October 2 in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia, alleging that the OCC exceeded its authority by issuing a rule and guidance allowing cryptocurrency companies to apply for limited national trust-bank charters; the suit sought revocation of the rule and related guidance. (Reuters, Oct. 2 08:21 ET)

## **UTHR** / **LQDA** [Pharma]
- A Delaware federal court ruled on September 30 that Liquidia Technologies induced infringement of United Therapeutics’ U.S. Patent No. 11,826,327 by marketing Yutrepia for pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease and found asserted claims 1 and 14 valid; the parties had until October 7 to submit a proposed final judgment, so no FDA-withdrawal order had been entered by October 5 at 12:20 ET. (Mugglehead, Oct. 4 10:57 ET)

## **TRI** / ROSS Intelligence [Software & SaaS]
- The Third U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled in Thomson Reuters’ favor in its copyright dispute with ROSS Intelligence, and ROSS said on October 2 that it would seek U.S. Supreme Court review; the litigation was unresolved as of October 5 at 12:20 ET. (LawNext, Oct. 2 19:09 ET)
